Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: a full-frame cinematic still for an original calm Japanese future-neighborhood film. Render a single 16:9 landscape image, no borders, no collage, no text overlay.
World: Tsugimachi (継町), an invented Japanese seaside hill town in the year 2080 — the same world as the supplied reference photographs (match their photographic look, light, color and material quality, but NOT their compositions). Society kept advancing technologically and chose to keep repairing its much-loved Showa-era buildings, appliances and habits. Old shopping lanes and hot-spring inns climb steep green slopes above a calm bay, like a Showa-era seaside resort town. Offshore lies Tsugishima (継島), a small island town enclosed by a high concrete seawall and packed with weathered 1960s concrete apartment blocks of 6–10 stories, stairways, rooftop gardens, a small shrine and a white lighthouse — dense like an old coal-mining island town, but lived-in, repaired and cared for, never ruined. Advanced buildings rise among the old blocks: rounded blue-tinted curved glass, pale ceramic structural ribs, planted terraces and slender skybridges, all clearly grounded on structures. White car-like four-seat flying passenger vehicles travel quietly along air corridors: rounded white ceramic-metal car bodies with a dark curved windshield and four clearly visible shrouded ring-shaped lift fans (ducted rotors) at the corners, no wheels, small navigation lights. Helper robots work alongside residents; they all share ONE design: about 1.3 m tall, smooth ivory ceramic shell with matte warm-grey joints, a rounded head with a single narrow horizontal amber light strip instead of a face (no eyes, no mouth), slim arms with simple three-finger hands, short legs, a small amber status light on the chest, a few replaced panels showing careful maintenance. They never resemble any existing character, mascot or trademark. It is an optimistic, quiet, ordinary late-summer Sunday (25 August 2080), not a disaster, not an abandoned city.
Visual language: a convincingly photographed location, cinematic naturalism. Pronounced foreground / middle ground / distance with an object or frame that partly occludes the foreground, a daily activity in the middle ground, and the next space continuing beyond. Realistic 28–35 mm perspective with straight structural lines, mostly in focus. Rich cobalt and cyan daylight, naturally saturated greens and sea blues, aged honey-brown wood, faded celadon enamel, cream plaster, restrained rusty ochre. Directional light and believable soft fill; protect highlights, keep shadow detail. Real wood grain, worn touch points, repaired paint, rippled old glass, woven cloth; old does not mean uniformly dirty. Fine photographic texture, no visible brushwork, no anime outlines, no waxy CGI, no oversharpened HDR, no cyberpunk neon.
Humans are incidental: seen from behind, from the side at a distance, or small in the frame; never a presenting host or a central close-up face. No trademarked characters, brand logos, watermarks, captions or explanatory slogans. Only the short Japanese signs explicitly requested may be readable, and they must be physically part of the scene.
Chapter-2 additions to the world: a slender suspended monorail (two rounded cars in white and fresh leaf-green hanging under a single thin elevated rail) glides between the glass towers and above the old tiled roofs. Familiar chain shops survive with their signboards, but only as this town's own invented shops: an orange-signed beef-bowl counter shop "牛丼 つぎ家", a convenience store "つぎマート" (white sign with colored stripes) and a classic coffee shop (純喫茶) — never any real brand name or logo. Craftsmen (plasterers, carpenters, scaffolders in helmets and baggy nikka-pokka trousers) work together with the helper robots and teach them their skills. The island has a small hilltop shrine with a weathered gray stone torii, stone lanterns and a huge ginkgo tree.
Recurring people (always seen from behind, from the side at a distance, or as hands only — never a face): THE MAN is about 50, in a dark navy business suit and white shirt, short graying hair, with a dark-brown leather briefcase. THE OLD ROBOT is the town's oldest helper robot: exactly the standard design, but clearly older — chipped ivory paint, several replaced panels in slightly different ivory tones, a small hand-painted number on its left shoulder. THE CHILD is about 8, in a dark-blue jinbei with a small RED hair clip. Vivid red is reserved for the child's hair clip; other reds in the scene stay muted (dull vermilion, brick, rust).
